## Analysis

**Plant part affected:** Seed/seedling (early stage disease)

**Key visual features:**
- Pale/whitish to tan rotted seed or early seedling
- Water-soaked, soft rot appearance
- Soil contact and adhesion
- Single affected structure in germination/early growth stage

**Candidate elimination:**
- **Phomopsis** (seed disease): Shows post-harvest cracked, dull seeds with gray mold - not matching the in-soil, water-soaked appearance
- **Purple_Seed_Stain** (seed disease): Seeds show purple/dark discoloration from hilum - test image lacks this characteristic coloring
- **Cercospora** (seed disease): Purple/brown seed coat discoloration - not visible in test image
- **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus** (seed disease): Mottled seed coats - not evident in test
- **Rhizoctonia** (root/seedling): Causes dry, firm, sunken cankers - test image shows soft, water-soaked rot instead
- **Fusarium** (seedling/root): Would show more advanced seedling development and wilting - test shows severely compromised early stage

**Best match: Pythium_damping_off**

The test image matches the symptom description precisely: "Infected seeds appear rotted with soil sticking to them; seedlings develop water-soaked lesions on the hypocotyl or cotyledons that become a brown soft rot." Reference views of Pythium_damping_off (particularly Soybean_Dise_45.jpg in seed stage and Soybean_Dise_12.jpg whole plant) showed nearly identical appearances with rotted seeds/seedlings in direct soil contact with soft decay. This is the classic early-stage damping-off presentation.
